text:
Emily: Quick heads-up — I ran the end-to-end endpoint profiling for the multi-tenant run last night and found a reproducible token-latency regression for tenant 'acme-inc' when seq_len > 1024. Looks like kernel selection flips to the slower attention kernel under certain batching conditions.

Ben: Can you paste the trace? Is it the kernel choice or batching queuing?

Emily: Both. The perf traces show a 30-60ms jump at the op boundary right when the batcher merges a long request with short ones. Kernel chooser switches to the fallback kernel because the estimated peak memory crosses the heuristic. Here's the snippet from the trace: 

```
# perf trace excerpt
op=attn_forward kernel=optim_blk16 fallback=true est_mem=5.2GB batch=[short,short,long] -> kernel_switch
latency_token_breakdown: kv_lookup=4ms compute=48ms kernel_switch=36ms postproc=2ms
```

Carla: That aligns with the KV cache telemetry I pulled — acme-inc had a KV miss-rate spike during the same window. Their prefix hit rate dropped from ~82% to 41% when we started merging long seqs into mixed batches. Misses cause more memory pressure because we allocate larger KV buffers transiently.

Ben: Oof. We need a per-tenant token-level latency dashboard and a per-route KPI so SRE/product can see which customers are hitting this. Right now everything aggregates across the org and hides spikes.

Dan: Agreed. Also add RBAC so customer success can view only their workspace KPIs; we should avoid exposing other tenants' traffic. Proposal: new "workspace_metrics" role with read-only access to dashboards scoped by workspace_id.

InfraBot: deploy-log: metrics-service v1.14.2 -> canary started at 1749001400, migration: add workspace_id label to token_latency and kv_* metrics.

Alice: I sketched a PromQL + Grafana panel idea:

```
# token-level p50/p95 per workspace
sum by (workspace_id) (rate(token_latency_seconds_sum{job="serving",workspace_id!=""}[5m])) /
sum by (workspace_id) (rate(token_latency_seconds_count{job="serving",workspace_id!=""}[5m]))
```

and for breakouts: kv_hit_rate per workspace
```
sum by (workspace_id) (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by (workspace_id) (rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
```

Emily: Nice. Also include a stacked token-latency breakdown panel with series: kv_lookup, kernel_compute, kernel_switch, postproc. That makes regressions instantly obvious.

Carla: For multi-tenant partitioning, we should consider a soft quota for KV transient allocations per workspace. If a workspace triggers >X transient_kv_allocs in Ys, we either delay batching for that workspace or isolate its batches to avoid cross-tenant kernel flips.

Ben: Can we simulate the suggested heuristics in staging? I want to see cost/regressions tradeoff before shipping.

Emily: I have a perf harness that replays ACME traces with exact seq lengths. I'll run two experiments: 1) current heuristic, 2) per-tenant isolation for long sequences. I'll record token-level breakdown and per-route success p99.

Dan: Add an experiment to the dashboards that overlays the baseline vs isolation run. Trace IDs should be attached to metrics via trace_id label so we can drill down.

InfraBot: alert: high_kv_miss_rate detected on tenant=acme-inc at 1749001503, threshold 0.3 exceeded (current 0.59). Notified: @carla @emily.

Carla: Thanks infra-bot. Running a quick KV TTL sweep to free transient state now. Also tweaking per-tenant cache sizing to 1.2x baseline for the next 30m to reduce misses.

Alice: One more thing — kernel chooser itself should emit the "chooser_reason" label (e.g., mem_estimate, seq_length, batch_mix) so dashboards can break down why a switch happened. That will help debug false positives when our heuristics are conservative.

Ben: Love that. Add to the metrics backlog and prioritize kernel_chooser labels + workspace scoping as P1 for the next sprint. Product wants visibility for a handful of pilot customers.

Emily: Plan: 1) run experiments (today) 2) add workspace labels and kernel_chooser reasons in staging (this week) 3) Grafana panels for per-tenant token-latency and kv hit-rate + stacked breakdown (next week) 4) RBAC dashboards (design doc). I'll post results once experiments finish.

Dan: For the RBAC doc, include examples of who gets the workspace_metrics role (CS, Sec, tenant admins) and audit events for dashboard views.

Ben: Thanks team. If experiments show isolation helps with <10% cost increase and removes p99 spikes, we can roll a soft default. Otherwise we revert and refine heuristics. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:

Emily: Will do. Starting the replay now — trace IDs: replay-174900-01 and replay-174900-02. I'll attach raw traces and perf logs when done.

Carla: I'm leaving a short follow-up in the metrics channel with the current kv partition proposal details.

Ben: Cool. Moving to action items in linear.
